name: ASSA ABLOY AB ser. B
executive_summary: ASSA ABLOY is a global leader in locks, access control, and security hardware, rated **Strong Buy** by the quantitative screen on quality, GARP, dividend growth, and risk metrics rather than deep value. The investment case rests on sustained organic growth, record margins, acquisition-led scale, and robust free cash flow (Piotroski F-Score 8/9), with valuation at P/E 24.2 and P/B 3.6 looking reasonable against ~16% earnings growth (PEGY 0.12) but far from Graham-style cheapness. The central debate is whether roll-up economics and margin expansion justify leverage-heavy balance sheet (net debt ~SEK 57bn, negative tangible equity) and thin liquidity (current ratio 1.03), especially after 2025 earnings and Q1 2026 showed a modest year-on-year softening. Primary filing bodies are absent from the research pack; figures below should be verified against ASSA ABLOY’s annual report and interim releases before trading.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s **Strong Buy** signal (composite 0.82, sector-relative 0.76, conviction 0.59 building over two weeks) is driven by five factor families: **cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk**. Eight models pass, including Neff PEGY (PEGY 0.12 on ~15.9% growth), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality — a profile consistent with a compounder trading at a growth-adjusted discount rather than an asset bargain.

Business quality indicators align with the screen: ROE 15.6%, operating cash flow ~SEK 21.4bn, and canonical FCF ~SEK 18.6bn (screen TTM ~USD 18.4bn) with OCF consistently exceeding net income (Piotroski cash-quality tests pass). Revenue has compounded from SEK 120.8bn (2022) to SEK 152.4bn (2025) per Yahoo, with gross margin expanding from ~39.7% to ~42.6% over the same period — consistent with pricing power and mix shift toward higher-value access solutions. Dividend growth is steady (cash dividends paid rose from SEK 4.7bn in 2022 to SEK 6.6bn in 2025), and news flow cites a proposed SEK 6.40/share dividend for 2025 alongside record EBIT margins at Q4 2025.

For a value investor, the name qualifies as **quality-at-a-fair-price GARP** rather than net-net or deep value: it fails Graham Defensive, Schloss Low P/B, Deep Value, FCF Yield (<5%), Lynch PEG (1.52), and Economic Moat screens (ROE below 18% threshold). The thesis is that ASSA ABLOY’s global installed base, specification-led sales channels, and bolt-on M&A engine create durable returns on invested capital that the screen’s growth-adjusted metrics capture better than static P/E or P/B alone.
financial_review:

Annual and interim analysis below therefore **falls back to Yahoo Finance (`financials_annual.json`)** and cached quarterly income. All figures stated as reported by Yahoo unless noted; currency appears to be **SEK millions**. This pack cannot cite going-concern language, segment detail, or management commentary from regulatory text.

**Profitability:** Gross margin improved steadily (39.7% → 42.6%), but operating margin peaked at ~16.3% in 2024 and eased to ~15.5% in 2025. Normalised income (Yahoo) was SEK 14.9bn in 2025 versus reported SEK 14.7bn, after SEK 328m restructuring/M&A charges — a recurring feature of the acquisition model.

**Cash conversion:** OCF exceeded net income in every year shown; capex remained modest (~SEK 2.4–2.8bn annually). FCF comfortably covers dividends (SEK 6.6bn paid in 2025) and bolt-on M&A, though **business purchases totalled SEK 11.4bn in 2025**, SEK 12.1bn in 2024, and SEK 53.6bn in 2023 (Yahoo cash-flow statement) — confirming the roll-up capital allocation model.

**Balance sheet / leverage:** Net debt/EBITDA approximates **~2.0×** (SEK 57.3bn / SEK 29.2bn EBITDA, Yahoo 2025). Debt-to-equity on the screen is 64.1%. Interest expense rose from SEK 919m (2022) to SEK 3.3bn (2025), reflecting higher gross debt. Current ratio **1.03** and working capital of SEK 1.5bn (down from SEK 5.3bn in 2024) signal **tight near-term liquidity** — consistent with the screen’s Financial Health model failure.

**Interim / quarterly (Yahoo cached; no indexed interim filing):** Yahoo quarterly income shows Q1 2026 revenue SEK 35.8bn and net income SEK 3.54bn versus Q1 2025 revenue SEK 38.0bn and net income SEK 3.81bn — a **~6% revenue and ~7% earnings decline** year-on-year in the most recent quarter available. News headlines (Feb 2026) cite Q4 2025 organic sales growth of 4% and record EBIT/EBITA margins, but without filing bodies this memo cannot reconcile full-year 2025 segment performance, APAC weakness, or FX impacts cited in the Q4 earnings-call headline.

**Gaps:** No annual report, half-year report, or trading update text is available in this pack. Segment mix, order backlog, covenant detail, pension obligations, and goodwill impairment testing cannot be verified from primary sources here.
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and M&A integration:** The balance sheet is structurally geared to acquisitions — goodwill plus intangibles exceed SEK 138bn against SEK 102bn equity (Yahoo 2025). Negative tangible book and sustained purchase-of-business outflows raise **goodwill impairment** and integration execution risk; a slowdown in organic growth could pressure returns on acquired assets.

**Liquidity:** Current ratio 1.03 and declining working capital warrant monitoring, especially if acquisition pace continues while cash balances are low (SEK 1.4bn at end-2025 per Yahoo). The screen explicitly flags weak liquidity.

**Earnings momentum:** Reported net income and EPS fell in FY2025 versus FY2024, and Yahoo Q1 2026 shows further YoY softness. Without interim filing commentary, the durability of “record margin” narrative (news, Feb 2026) versus top-line deceleration is unresolved.

**Cyclical / geographic exposure:** Q4 2025 earnings-call coverage notes challenges in APAC and foreign-exchange impacts. Construction and commercial retrofit cycles affect mechanical and electromechanical lock volumes; macro context is not used to override the screen but construction softness remains a plausible headwind.

**Competitive / structural:** The global locks and access-control market is fragmented but consolidating; ASSA ABLOY competes with Dormakaba, Allegion, and regional players. Technology shift toward cloud access and IoT could require sustained R&D (SEK 6.9bn in 2025 per Yahoo) to defend share.

**Governance / regulatory:** No filing bodies available to assess related-party transactions, auditor emphasis-of-matter paragraphs, or going-concern statements. Dual-listing (OMX Stockholm; ADR ASAZY/ASAZF) adds cross-border disclosure complexity not resolved in this pack.

**Pension:** Yahoo balance sheet shows current pension/post-retirement obligations of SEK 6.0bn (2025) and long-term provisions; magnitude and funding status cannot be assessed without the annual report note disclosures.

research_rationale: Quantitative quality/GARP signals are directionally supported by strong FCF, dividend growth, and margin expansion in Yahoo data and earnings headlines, but the absent primary filings, 2025 earnings dip, tight liquidity, and acquisition-heavy balance sheet prevent full confirmation of the Strong Buy case.
